title: Inequality, Education and Occupational Change in the Philippines
tldr: The Philippines' slow expansion in college-educated workers has maintained high wage premiums, sustaining inequality despite declining Gini coefficients, while emerging occupational polarization threatens recent gains.
problem_and_motivation: Despite sustained economic growth and declining poverty in the Philippines, wage inequality remains among the highest in Southeast Asia. The relationship between educational attainment, occupational structure, and wage distribution remains underexplored, particularly regarding how skill supply and employment composition have shaped wage gaps over the past two decades.
approach: Analysis of Philippine Labour Force Survey data (2002-2024) using RIF (Recentered Influence Function) regressions of unconditional quantiles of log real weekly wage income. Construction of occupation crosswalk harmonizing PSOC versions. Kernel density reweighting technique (DFL) to isolate impact of occupational reallocation on wage trends. Classification of occupations into high-skill, middle-skill routine, middle-skill nonroutine, and low-skill categories.
findings: The college wage premium remained persistently high (80% in 2024), driven by slow growth in college-educated workers. Returns to college education and high-skill occupations increase monotonically across the wage distribution, benefiting higher-income workers disproportionately. Between 2012-2016, middle-skilled job growth contributed to narrowing wage inequality. Recent trends (2016-2024) show declining middle-skilled employment and early signs of occupational polarization, though it remains unclear if structural or cyclical.

key_equations.College_wage_premium: Ratio of composition-adjusted mean log wages for college graduates to high school graduates estimated annually

definitions.College wage premium: Wage gap between college graduates and high school graduates, serving as proxy for market's valuation of skills
definitions.RIF regression: Recentered Influence Function regression for analyzing unconditional quantiles of wage distribution
definitions.Occupational polarization: Pattern where employment grows in both high-skill and low-skill occupations while declining in middle-skill occupations
definitions.Skill premium: The wage premium associated with higher education levels relative to lower education levels
definitions.DFL decomposition: DiNardo-Fortin-Lemieux kernel density reweighting technique to isolate impact of compositional changes on wage distribution

limitations: Wage data only available from 2002 onwards, limiting analysis period
LFS only publishes wage data starting 2002, restricting historical comparison
Income Gini data from FIES available only every 3 years (every 2 years since 2021), requiring interpolation
Analysis focuses only on wage workers, excluding self-employed and family workers
Cannot definitively determine whether recent middle-skilled employment decline is structural or cyclical
